thread.title: DSG approves over $70,000 in funding requests in first meeting of the year
thread.title_full: DSG approves over $70,000 in funding requests in first meeting of the year

author: Jeremiah Fang
title: DSG approves over $70,000 in funding requests in first meeting of the year
text:
Duke Student Government commenced its first senate meeting of the 2025-26 academic year Wednesday. During the meeting, DSG confirmed appointments to the Information Technology Advisory Council and approved student organization funding requests.
“I'm so excited to see what the session brings,” said DSG President Tara Singh, a senior.
The senators confirmed five new representatives for the Information Technology Advisory Council — a committee that advises Duke IT leadership on tech usage in academic settings. Juniors Angela Chen, Angeline Smith and Samanyu Gangappa and sophomores Ty Mastrian and Raahim Hashmi were confirmed at the session.
With club events in full swing on campus, the Student Organization Finance Committee (SOFC) approved more than $70,000 in funding requests.
SOFC is an independent branch of DSG that distributes the university’s near-$1 million student fund among its more than 250 student groups. Every week, the SOFC supervises the programming fund, which is open to all recognized student groups to fund events on campus. Once a semester, the SOFC taps into the operational and capital funds, financing closed- and open-membership student groups.
Senators approved the following OCF and programming requests.
MEDesign: $2,351 out of its requested $2,375 to cover for equipment, supplies and conference registration costs.
Business Oriented Women: $1,782 out of its requested $3,563 for conference-related lodging costs.
Duke Rhydun: $3,175 out of its requested $4,450 to cover space rental, food and personnel costs.
Dhamaka: $4,700 out of its requested $7,700 to cover outfit, personnel and transportation costs.
Duke Climbing Club: $3,000 out of its requested $7,500 to cover member pass costs.
National Society of Black Engineers: $9,700 out of its requested $10,674 to cover conference-related hotel and travel costs.
DJ@Duke: $2,269 funded in full to cover club costs.
Duke Mock Trial: $3,763 out of its requested $28,476 to cover travel costs for one of their five conferences; requested funding to cover their other four conferences were denied per SOFC guidelines instituted last year.
Duke Deewana: $6,660 out of its requested $17,928 to cover conference-related travel and photoshoot costs.
Black Pre-Law Society: $6,900 out of its requested $13,688 to cover conference-related travel and personnel costs.
Motorsports: $10,000 out of its requested $20,722 to cover facility upgrade and equipment costs.
Society of Women Engineers: $10,000 out of its requested $19,233 to cover conference-related travel and lodging costs.
Duke CommuniTea: $1,550 funded in full to cover tea, snack and equipment costs.
Muslim Student Association: $1,970 out of its requested $3,070 to cover catering costs.
Duke NROTC: $3,322 out of its requested $4,362 to cover guest speaker and snack costs.
